clue.text: Changes must be made in more stages where fuel is stored

indicators.note: the clue says the letters of the following words must be changed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction that the stages of a fuel depot must be reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes must be made in' tells you to rearrange MORE STAGES. Gasometers were the huge tanks that held town gas in British towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasometers are large storage tanks for gas, a fuel, so they are places where fuel is kept.

clue.text: Almost explode foolish mistake

indicators.note: almost means the phrase is used without its final letter

parts.note: to go off is to explode, as a bomb does

explanation.surface: Nearly blowing up through a silly error.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is a silly blunder.

clue.text: Pay, if sent, will be specially dealt with for security reasons

indicators.note: the letters given are to be dealt with in a special way, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: Wages sent out will be handled with care for security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be specially dealt with' rearranges PAY IF SENT. The definition is loose: a safety pin is fastened with a guard for safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin has a clasp covering its point so it fastens securely without pricking.

clue.text: People about 50 love fruit

indicators.note: about means the people go around the next pieces

parts.note: men are people
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Folk of around fifty who love fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large juicy fruit of the gourd family.

clue.text: Examine a note with a will

parts.note: to test is to examine
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Inspecting a memo with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a will' suggests energy, but in law it means having made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone testate died leaving a valid legal will.

clue.text: Hurried around a maniac-fast!

indicators.note: around means the word for hurried surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: ran means hurried
used as an adjective, maniac means mad

explanation.surface: Someone rushing round a lunatic at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but means a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month in which Muslims fast from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: A mineral in great demand by teetotal car-drivers

indicators.note: the word is wanted by, so held within, the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A mineral that teetotal motorists cannot get enough of.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside teetoTAL Car-drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral, magnesium silicate, ground to make talcum powder.

clue.text: Excited atmosphere surrounding a good fellow

indicators.note: surrounding means the atmosphere goes around the good fellow

parts.note: air is the atmosphere
ST stands for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A lively mood around a decent chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means stirring, up and about, in a state of excitement.

clue.text: Reading maketh a full man; a ready man; and writing an exact man 'Bacon (Essays)

definitions.text: Reading maketh a full man; a ready man; and writing an exact man 'Bacon (Essays)

parts.words: Reading maketh a full man; a ready man; and writing an exact man 'Bacon (Essays)
parts.note: a quotation from Francis Bacon's essay Of Studies with one word missing: what makes a man ready, between reading and writing

explanation.walkthrough: The full quotation is 'Reading maketh a full man; ___ a ready man; and writing an exact man.' The missing word, meaning discussion, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bacon's sense, talk and discussion with others makes a person quick-witted and ready.

clue.text: Pole fired and disregarded

parts.note: S is south, one of the earth's poles
lighted means set on fire

explanation.surface: A Polish man who was sacked and ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but gives S, for the south pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To be slighted is to be snubbed or treated with disdain.

clue.text: Refuse a king left behind

indicators.note: behind places the letter for left after the king's name

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke

explanation.surface: A command to decline, leaving a monarch in the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun (rubbish). OFFA was an Anglo-Saxon king of Mercia.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is waste parts, entrails and scraps, so it is rubbish in the noun sense of refuse.

clue.text: One's backing a politician to reveal the source of dope

indicators.note: backing turns the letters for one's round so they read the other way

parts.note: one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving I and S
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
to let on is to reveal or disclose

explanation.surface: A politician being backed up while disclosing where a drug came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IS into SI; then come MP and LET ON. 'Dope' in the surface means a drug, but here it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, a fool, which is exactly what a simpleton is.

clue.text: Flag to set by a road

parts.note: to set something down is to stand it

explanation.surface: A banner being put up beside a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner or flag, such as the royal standard flown over a palace.

clue.text: Eat too much Cheddar for example

definitions.meaning: to stuff yourself greedily with food
Cheddar in Somerset, England, is famous for a deep limestone ravine as well as its cheese

explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to overeat, and Cheddar Gorge is a famous ravine in Somerset, England.

clue.text: Fought over metal container, creating a racket

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: battled means fought
ore is rock that contains metal

explanation.surface: A fight over a tin can, causing a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests noise but is the bat. A battledore is the bat of the old game battledore and shuttlecock.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is a small racket used to hit a shuttlecock.

clue.text: Favours a really quiet ramble

definitions.note: the clue's verb is in the third person while the answer is the base form

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
to rove is to wander or ramble

explanation.surface: Someone likes a very quiet stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: In music, p means quiet and pp means very quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve of something is to look on it favourably, to favour it.

clue.text: Remaining true, maybe make a proposal

parts.note: over means left over, remaining

indicators.note: maybe signals that the word true is one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Staying faithful while possibly popping the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges TRUE into TURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an opening approach or offer made to start negotiations.

clue.text: A VIP turning on the board

indicators.note: turning means the little word on is read backwards

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging or a festive board

explanation.surface: A big shot sitting on the company board.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of distinction, an important figure like a VIP.

clue.text: Crowd returns to bar with fellow's bass tuba

indicators.note: returns means the word for crowd is turned round

parts.note: a mob is a crowd
a don is a fellow of a university college; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A crowd heading back to the pub with a man's tuba.
explanation.definitionFit: The bombardon is a large low-pitched brass instrument, a type of bass tuba.

clue.text: Brown, a common man, won't cross the line

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
gent, short for gentleman, is a colloquial word for a man

explanation.surface: A man called Brown who keeps strictly within the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname. The definition is descriptive: a tangent touches a curve without crossing it.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent meets a curve at a single point and does not cut through it.

clue.text: Eminent poet disconcerted about nothing being returned

indicators.note: about means the rearranged poet surrounds the next piece
disconcerted suggests the letters of poet are thrown into disorder
being returned means the word for nothing is reversed

parts.note: nil is nothing

explanation.surface: A famous poet upset about receiving nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminent' looks like a description of the poet but is the definition. 'disconcerted' scrambles the poet to TOPE, and the backwards nothing (LIN, via 'being returned') sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-line means of the highest rank, leading or most prominent.

clue.text: Eradicate mice possibly in a particular area

parts.note: to end something is to wipe it out

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word mice may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Wiping out the mice that may be found in one district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells you to rearrange MICE into EMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endemic is native to or found only within a certain region or population.

clue.text: A pledge that's quite serious

definitions.meaning: a token payment made as a guarantee

explanation.definitionFit: An earnest is a deposit or token given as a guarantee, and being earnest means being sincere and serious.

clue.text: Before the court-not bent though!

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
CT is an abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Appearing before a judge without being corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' in British slang means corrupt, which suits the court picture; here it simply means crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means upright and straight, the opposite of bent or crooked.

clue.text: Not all nurses can give the required anaesthetic

indicators.note: nurses in the sense of holds or cradles, so the words give the required contain the answer

explanation.surface: Not every nurse can administer the anaesthetic needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like the medical staff but signals that 'give the required' holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was one of the earliest general anaesthetics used in surgery.

clue.text: He'll support the worker after parking

indicators.note: after puts the worker following the letter for parking

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A man who will back the labourer once he has found a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a committed supporter of a cause or party.

clue.text: Absolutely perfect, thought the novice

parts.note: an idea is a thought
L stands for learner, a novice, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A beginner thought it was flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain learner drivers display an L plate, so L means a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes something that is perfect, the best that could be imagined.

clue.text: It's available -and the price is about right!

indicators.note: is about means the price goes around the next letter

parts.note: a fee is a price charged

explanation.surface: Something on offer at a fair price.
explanation.walkthrough: A wry joke: when something is free, the price is very right.
explanation.definitionFit: Free means available without restriction or without cost.

clue.text: Differently treated white rose

indicators.note: treated suggests the words white rose are worked on and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A white rose given some treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in another way, in a different manner.

clue.text: Duck that is sent back by the German

indicators.note: sent back means the abbreviation for that is is read in reverse

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is (id est)
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A bird returned by a German.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck whose soft down fills eiderdowns.

clue.text: Peer calling for listening equipment and money to be provided

parts.note: the ear is the organ we hear with
L stands for pound, from Latin libra, as in the pound sign

explanation.surface: A lord calling for headphones and cash to be supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb (look closely) but is a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Plague coppers standing around some steps

indicators.note: standing around means the coins go on either side of the steps

parts.note: coppers are low-value coins such as pence
a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence

explanation.surface: Police officers loitering near a flight of steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police but means copper coins. A stile is a step or steps over a fence on a British country path.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence is a deadly epidemic disease, a plague.
